why: Runs of equal characters are found with two pointers: i marks the start of a run and j walks right while the character stays the same. Every run is visited once, and using >= when comparing lengths keeps the rightmost longest run.
hints: Break the string into maximal blocks of one repeated character. How do you find where each block ends?
Set j = i and advance j while source[j] == source[i]; the run length is j - i, then jump i to j. Track the best run; on a tie the later run should win.
One linear scan with two indices, O(n) time and O(1) space; return best_char + str(best_len).
pitfalls: Ties go to the rightmost run: compare with >=, not >.
The answer is the character followed by the length as a string ("c3"), not the substring itself.
The final run ends at the end of the string; make sure it is compared too.
